text:
morgan: Heads up — noticed P99 for /v1/generate dropped to almost 0 in the dashboard right after the routing fallback we flipped at 11:12. Feels like the fallback route is being merged into the parent endpoint rollup and wiping the tail.

sanjay: hmm, that's unexpected. Which dashboard are you looking at? endpoint="/v1/generate" or the route-level view?

morgan: endpoint-level. The route-level p99 still shows the spike on the canary route but endpoint p99 goes flat.

elaine: could be the sampling merge we added last quarter — when route tags are present we do a weighted rollup, and if the fallback route has low sample count we were previously dropping it from tdigest merge. I thought we added a guard for extreme tails though.

morgan: I pulled the raw counts from telemetry: ``samples: { main: 4200, canary: 12, fallback: 3 }`` — fallback has tiny count but VERY high latency (1.2s). The rollup seems to ignore it.

rachel: deploy-bot: config change applied by @elaine at 2024-10-07T11:12Z — routing policy: enable-fallback-merge=true

deploy-bot: rollout complete for policy/route-fallbacks v2.1 :white_check_mark:

elaine: ah right, that merge mode had a threshold: we skip including samples if route_count < 10 to avoid noisy extremes. That explains fallback being excluded from tdigest merge so aggregate p99 drops.
sanjay: but excluding small counts can hide real tail regressions for small but critical routes (e.g., retries/fallbacks). We need a way to surface those without polluting noise.

morgan: agreed. For product traffic, even a few slow fallback calls matter. Suggestions?

elaine: two options: 1) Always include route samples when latency > X ms (i.e., treat high-latency small-sample as signal), or 2) surface a separate "rare-route-tail" metric that shows p99 across low-sample routes.
rachel: can we just annotate endpoint dashboards with a "hidden-samples" count that warns when we're dropping tiny-route samples? That'd be lower effort.
sanjay: annotation helps, but ops need an alert when a small route shows huge p99. Otherwise it slips by. We could add a rule: if any child route p99 > threshold and child_count >= 1, raise an "endpoint-heterogeneity" alert.

morgan: alert rule sounds good. Also need UX on console so SREs can click to expand and see child routes and raw latencies, not only merged tdigest. The current hover only shows p50/p95/p99 with no breakdown.

elaine: agree. I'll open a tracking ticket: - change merge behavior to include samples if latency percentile > 750ms even if count < 10 - add dashboard annotation when samples are dropped - add alert rule for child-route p99 > 500ms with count >=1
sanjay: add one more: store a lightweight sample-backed "rare-route" histogram with lower retention so we can inspect without storing full payloads.
rachel: +1 on low-retention histogram. Also update docs: explain why endpoint p99 can be lower than all child p99s (caused by exclusion). Took me a bit to reason through it.

morgan: I can paste the quick query I used to find raw buckets: ``SELECT route, count, approx_quantile(latency_ms, 0.99) FROM telemetry.raw_requests WHERE endpoint='/v1/generate' AND ts > now() - INTERVAL '1 hour' GROUP BY route;``

elaine: perfect — can you attach screenshot of the endpoint dashboard snippet? that helps product.
morgan: attaching in thread.

rachel: plan sounds solid. Next steps: (1) @elaine file RFC + ticket for merge tweak and annotation (2) @sanjay add alert rule in prometheus/alerts (3) @morgan add dashboard expansion mockups (4) ops to test with synthetic small-sample high-latency injection tomorrow at 09:00 PT.

morgan: noted. I'll run the synthetic job and post results. :thumbsup:

elaine: rolling this into next sprint. Thanks for catching it.

sanjay: thanks — this will save us from silent tail regressions on fallbacks/retries. :rocket:
